evidence: The base image named by the repository's Dockerfile carries no CRITICAL OS-level vulnerabilities — the packages the app manifest never declares
expected_output: grype-report.json; one observation row per match with vulnerability, severity, package, version, fix_state, image

assertions.description: Zero CRITICAL vulnerabilities in the final stage's base image.

caveats: M1 scans the base image the final FROM names, not a locally built app image; unevidenced when there is no Dockerfile or the image cannot be pulled.
notes: Empty-set discipline — Skip: with no image to scan the collector skips with a stated reason and the recipe stays unevidenced; when it does run, every package grype resolves in the image is matched against the whole pinned vulnerability database, so an empty finding set is an exhaustively searched clean result.

plain.checks: Takes the base image your Dockerfile builds on and scans the operating-system packages inside it for known critical vulnerabilities — the software your application's dependency manifest never mentions.
plain.violation: The image you ship carries a known-critical hole in something you did not choose and do not list: a system library, a shell, a TLS package. It is present in every running container regardless of how clean your own dependencies are.
plain.fix: Rebuild on the current tag of the same base image, or move to a smaller image that carries less. Each finding names the package and the version that fixes it; where no fixed version exists yet, that is a decision to record rather than a result to ignore.
